why: Touching both axes in the first quadrant forces centre (a, a) and radius a; (3-a)^2 + (6-a)^2 = a^2 gives a^2 - 18a + 45 = 0, so a = 3 or 15, and a = 3 yields x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 6y + 9 = 0.
The diameters meet at the centre (1, -1); area 154 with pi = 22/7 gives r^2 = 49, so (x-1)^2 + (y+1)^2 = 49 expands to x^2 + y^2 - 2x + 2y = 47.
Centre (h, 4h-3) equidistant from (2,3) and (4,5) gives 20h = 40, h = 2, so centre (2,5) and r^2 = 4, i.e. x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 10y + 25 = 0.
For x + 2y = c the distance |c|/sqrt(5) must equal the radius 2, giving c = +/- 2*sqrt(5); substituting confirms a zero discriminant (double root), whereas c = +/- 2*sqrt(3) gives discriminant 32.
The two lines are parallel (6x - 8y - 7 = 0 normalises to 3x - 4y - 7/2 = 0); their separation |4 + 7/2|/5 = 3/2 is the diameter, so the radius is 3/4.
Passing through the origin forces c = 0, then g = -a/2 and f = -b/2, so the centre (-g, -f) is (a/2, b/2); this point is verified equidistant (a^2/4 + b^2/4) from all three given points.

In an equilateral triangle the centroid divides the median 2:1 and coincides with the circumcentre, so R = (2/3)(3a) = 2a; explicit vertices at radius 2a were checked to have median exactly 3a, giving x^2 + y^2 = 4a^2.
Half-angle 30 degrees gives OA = 2 and tangent length sqrt(3), so the kite OPAQ has area sqrt(3); subtracting the 120-degree sector pi/3 leaves sqrt(3) - pi/3 = 0.6849, matching only option B.
The circle has centre (-m/2, -m/2) and radius |m|/sqrt(2); substituting option A into x^2 + y^2 + mx + my gives identically 0 for all theta, while B and D leave non-zero residuals.
